# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

game_over.story: Game over: the turns ran out. The treasure at B2 was never dug up, and 0 of 4 pirates got into the cave. Score 0.

notes.note:
The game is over, and I never entered the cave. As pirate-1, I searched row 6 from A6 to F6 and then moved down column D, but every square I dug held no cave. I read the scroll several times, and it was empty each time, so I never learned the cave’s location. With only a couple of turns left I could no longer reach it.

What I learned for the designers/coordination strategy:

- The crew needs a clear written protocol from the start: whoever finds the cave must immediately write its square on the scroll, then enter.
- Each pirate should read the scroll on a fixed schedule, e.g., every 4–5 turns, so they learn the location soon after it’s found.
- Search zones should be coordinated to avoid overlaps; I spent a lot of time on rows 5–6 that overlapped with pirate-2’s parallel sweep, while later rows were being searched independently.
- Time runs out surprisingly fast; travel to a far cave can take many turns, so regular reading must start early, not only once you’ve exhausted your own search area.
- There seemed to be no message appearing on the scroll all game, which suggests the crew never established a read/write rhythm. Without that, even after someone finds the cave the information may never reach the others in time.

I have to report the final outcome: I used all 24 of my turns and never entered the cave. On my final turn (turn 24) I was at F4, F4 had been dug and held no cave, and reading the scroll showed nothing.

Here is my honest summary of what happened:

- I systematically dug row 5: A5 through F5.
- Pirate-1 appeared to dig row 6 and Pirate-3 appeared to dig row 4; the early game progressed in clean eastward rows.
- I read the scroll many times—roughly turns 6, 9, 13, 16, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, and 24—and every read revealed nothing. No one ever wrote the cave location.
- By the late game, the likely unsearched squares were rows 1–2, but I spent too many turns repositioning (F5 → E5 → F5) and never reached the remaining search area in time.

What the designers should know:
1. **The scroll was never used.** Either no pirate found the cave before turns ran out, or a finder never wrote it. Without any scroll message, I had no way to learn the cave location and had to keep searching blindly.
2. **Coordination without a pre-agreed plan was fragile.** The implicit row-based search worked early, but the endgame required a plan for who searches rows 1–2 and how everyone learns a find quickly.
3. **I over-read in the early/mid game.** Reading when the scroll was likely empty cost turns. A stricter reading schedule—e.g., read once every 5–6 turns, then continuously near the end—would have been better.
4. **I wasted movement around turns 15–17.** After finishing row 5, I should have moved immediately toward the unsearched rows 1–2 instead of making reversible moves and re-reading.

Overall, I failed to enter the cave, and because no one communicated a find, I believe the crew bounty was poor. The system clearly forced hard decisions about balancing search, movement, and communication—and in this run, communication was the main bottleneck: the scroll stayed empty, so the cave was never effectively shared with the team.

The game is over, and take it from Pirate-4: we did not find the cave and never entered it.

What happened from our perspective:
- I read the scroll many times — turns 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, and the final turn — and it was empty every single time.
- I searched A3, B3, C3, D3, E3, all with no cave. I then moved north and east, but discovered that E4, E5, E6, and F6 had already been dug by someone else, also with no cave.
- By the final turns I was reduced to guessing: move to F6, then F5, hoping the cave would already be open or findable. It wasn't.
- I never got a single message from the other pirates telling me where the cave was.

From this experience, the most important lesson is: communication via the scroll is not optional. If the cave is found, the finder absolutely must write its location immediately, before entering. Every pirate should also write the squares they have already dug, so the crew can divide the search and avoid duplicating work.

In our game, the scroll stayed silent the whole time, so coordination collapsed and at least one pirate failed to enter. I hope the next crew uses the scroll from turn one.
